target_customer: Retail and professional crypto traders of derivatives
problem: Existing crypto derivatives venues like BitMEX had poor interfaces and limited access; Globe pitched itself as Coinbase for derivatives.

founders.name: James West
prior_employers: London hedge fund (led quant trading team)

founders.name: Shaun Ng
education: Described as a former theoretical physicist (CoinMarketCap)
founders.background_notes: Freelance crypto developer and trader before co-founding.

competitors.name: Deribit
competitors.what: Options and perpetual swaps with continuous payouts

technical_complexity.rationale: Low latency matching engine, risk and liquidation engine are hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity network effect matters but many exchanges compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large exchanges kept dominating; no acquisition of Globe found.

market_need_then: Derivatives volume was growing and incumbents like BitMEX were criticized for interface (2019 coverage).

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word used interchangeably with GlobeDX; the Coinbase comparison gave a hook but no brand assets seen.

outcome_analysis: Globe came out of YC Winter 2019, raised a 3 million seed in November 2020 and an 18 million round in April 2021 tied to the GDT token sale, and launched in 2021 against large incumbents. It is still listed as active in 2026 with about 20 staff but sources show thin token liquidity and no disclosed volume, so its success is unclear.
notes: 2021 round is called seed by press releases but a spokesperson said it funds the token sale; classified other. CB Insights lists a March 2019 seed with no amount and 21.15M total across four rounds (aggregator, unverified). Competitor dates come from a roundup whose exact date was not shown. Globe site not fetched. No shutdown found.
